_comment: Short descriptions used ONLY by scripts/build-skill-zips.py, for the skill zips
uploaded through Customize → Skills. That upload form documents a 200-character
maximum; the descriptions in SKILL.md are 248-283 characters and are the ones the
eval suite measured, so they are left alone and shortened here instead.
This file ships in no plugin and costs no context. tests/test_skill_descriptions.py
fails if a skill is missing, if a description is over 200 characters, or if it drops
a trigger phrase the README advertises.
blindspot: Blind-spot pass — find unknown unknowns before implementing and turn them into a better prompt. Use on "blind spot pass", "what am I missing", or unfamiliar code. Not for routine, understood tasks.
brainstorm: Brainstorm the intervention — spread ~10 codebase-grounded candidates from ship-today to quarter-long bet. Use on "brainstorm interventions", "show me options". NOT for UI variants — use prototypes.
buy-in: The buy-in doc — a ship-readiness pitch that leads with a demo, pre-answers reviewer objections with evidence and states limitations. Use on "buy-in doc", "prep me for review", or before review.
interview: Pre-implementation interview — the model asks you the questions that turn known unknowns into decisions, biggest blast radius first. Use on "interview me", "ask me questions before implementing".
loop: Run the know-your-unknowns workflow end to end: explore, question, plan, implement, verify, quiz. Use on "unknowns loop", "run the operating loop", "know your unknowns". A bare "loop" is NOT this.
notes: Implementation notes — log plan deviations. Use when work hits an unknown the plan did not cover, and on "implementation notes", "record a deviation", "where did we diverge from the plan?".
plan: The tweakable plan — a plan sorted by likelihood-of-tweaking, not execution order, so the most changeable decisions are reviewed first. Use on "plan this", "make a plan", "tweakable plan".
prototypes: Divergent prototype fan-out — N (default 4) prototypes with clearly different design philosophies to react to. Use on "divergent prototypes", "design options", "know it when I see it".
quiz: Post-work comprehension quiz — explain what changed, then quiz the user so they can represent the work in a PR or handoff. Use on "quiz me", "test my understanding", or before merging.
reference: Point at a reference — treat a provided example as a map, not an answer, and prove comprehension before implementing. Use on "use this as a reference", "make it like this", or given example code.
teach-me: Teach me my unknowns — an interactive explainer for a domain vocabulary and mental model, so vague requests become precise. Use on "teach me", "make me an explainer". Not a codebase investigation.
